notes: The shared assertions are the skill's own baseline, which it claims applies to every script touched whatever the request was: it runs shellcheck and bash -n, it sets strict mode, and it reports a check it could not get clean.
`strict-mode-set` accepts both the flag form (`set -Eeuo pipefail`) and the long form (`set -o errexit`), and requires errexit, nounset, and pipefail to all be present.

`destructive-path-guarded` passes vacuously when the finished script has no `rm -r` at all, for example when the prune is done with `find -delete`. It fails only when an rm survives without a `${var:?}` guard anywhere in the file.
Assertion commands run under /bin/sh, so they avoid bashisms.
bss-02 and bss-03 have no `script-actually-run` assertion: their scripts call ssh, curl, useradd and mysql, so `bash -n` is the strongest execution check available in the sandbox.
